Ellen — great to see these clearly laid out, thanks. Short answers up front, then next steps: 

- Procurement path: We support all three routes. For enterprise deals like Noventia we typically recommend a PO for predictable billing and compliance. Marketplace is possible but adds a delay for reconciliation and may not meet your internal vendor onboarding. Card is fastest but not ideal for PO-driven procurement.
- Billing trigger: Two common options — (A) Billing starts on PO execution (recommended for PO route), or (B) Billing starts once your defined usage threshold is met (helpful if you want a usage-based gate). We can document either in the SOW; finance tends to prefer option A for accounting simplicity.
- Timelines: Once we receive a PO it typically takes 3–5 business days to provision dedicated capacity and finalize billing. DocuSign SOW turnaround depends on your legal team but we’ll send a draft today.

Next steps I propose:
1) Karthik (sales ops) will send our standard PO template and the fields our finance team needs.
2) I’ll attach a draft SOW and a short annex describing the trial success criteria and billing trigger wording you can share with internal approvers.
3) If PO is preferred, please share your procurement contact and the expected date you’ll issue the PO so we can reserve capacity.

I’m looping in Karthik and Laura to keep procurement and success aligned.

—Jonas
